title: From Jupyter to Production 🚀
description: Why 90% of models never see daylight — and how to bridge the gap between a notebook and a live system.

slides.title: The Last Mile Problem 🏁
slides.content:
# Model Deployment

Training a great model in a notebook is only half the battle. The other half is **deployment**: making the model available to users or other systems in a reliable, scalable way.

- Deployment transforms your static `.pkl` file into a living service.
- It bridges data science and software engineering.

Studies show that up to 90% of ML models never make it to production — often due to engineering gaps, not model quality.

slides.title: Notebook vs Production 🌉
slides.content:
# Different Worlds

| Notebook | Production |
|----------|------------|
| Ad‑hoc run | Always‑on service |
| Small static data | Streaming real‑time data |
| Manual steps | Automated pipelines |
| Researcher mindset | Engineering robustness |

In production, you must handle versioning, monitoring, error handling, latency requirements, and security.

quizData.question: Why do many ML models never reach production?

options.text: The engineering effort to deploy, monitor, and maintain them is often underestimated
Models are too large to store

quizData.explanation: Deployment requires robust software engineering practices that data science projects may lack.

slides.title: Deployment Strategies 🗺️
slides.content:
# Common Patterns

- **Batch prediction**: run model on a schedule (e.g., nightly scoring). Simple, no real‑time needs.
- **Real‑time API**: model served behind a REST/gRPC endpoint. Latency matters.
- **Edge deployment**: model runs on device (phone, IoT). Requires model compression (e.g., TensorFlow Lite).

Choice depends on use case: fraud detection needs real‑time; customer churn prediction can be batch.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Start Simple
Deploy your first model as a simple Flask/FastAPI endpoint inside a Docker container. That’s enough for many applications and teaches you the fundamentals.
